6. Strongest companion results

The technical companion preserves several further completed constructions.

 | Result | What is established | What remains outside it

 | Exact logical-excursion representation | Eliminating syndrome excursions can retain their logical Pauli action and physical duration. A conservative accelerated-killing bound gives a complete-channel retention certificate. | No efficient evaluation or useful release-average estimate for the full acquired release class.

 | Native QND monitoring under the same bath | Chosen local check controls preserve a Pauli-times-stabilizer-function trajectory algebra, including nonunitary no-jump factors and arbitrary CPTP primitive faults on marked supports. | Finite noncommuting Bell/gate pulses require a separate bath analysis.

 | Explicit space-time neutralization decoder | Exact local GF(2) solves, a deterministic geometric correctness proof, a computable threshold under its positive marked-support law, and a coherent initial-history extension. | This is not the overall processor threshold or a physically completed decoding service.

 | Measured terminal boundary and parity compression | Actual Bell/readout records close the detector algebra. Completed local corrections contribute only two logical parity bits per qubit. | Unfinished local decoding jobs still need paid routing, storage, service and latency.

The excursion result is particularly useful for avoiding a false inference from syndrome mixing. If $Q^0$ is the actual process killed at its first nontrivial dressed logical jump, and $A$ is a chosen syndrome region with complement $B$, its killed trace generator is

$$S
=
Q^0_{AA}
+
Q^0_{AB}(-Q^0_{BB})^{-1}Q^0_{BA},$$

assuming the eliminated restriction is transient.

For the unnormalized release mass $\mu_A$,

$$\Pr(\text{first logical fault by physical time }t)
\le
1-\mu_Ae^{tS}\mathbf1.$$

The trace process deletes time spent in $B$, charging fatal excursions early. This makes the inequality conservative without assuming that excursions have already returned by the physical deadline. It retains logical return-loop effects that a scalar syndrome gap can miss. Its matrices can still be exponentially large.
